audit.why: 42.6% Emerald+ is the lowest figure in this slice and the page's shape explains it honestly: Ryze bullies levels 2-3, Kassadin owns 4-5 through first item, and then Ryze out-scales him again. It is the rare matchup where Kassadin does not win by waiting, and both layers already say so.

audit.whatIsWrong: Every one of the seven win[] entries read 'Skill' and every phases[].side read 'Skill' — a flat chart on a matchup whose own captions describe four separate swings. whys[1] and whys[2] hand Ryze levels 2 and 3, whys[3] says 'you out-last his trades', whys[4] calls Level 6 'your first real window', whys[5] says 'you trade even or better', and whys[6] says flatly 'Ryze hard-outscales you'.
audit.why: A chart that says Skill at every stage tells the reader nothing, and here it actively hides the most important fact in the matchup — that Kassadin's advantage is a mid-game window that closes again once Ryze finishes Seraph's.
audit.corrected: Level 1 stays Skill; Levels 2 and 3 to Ryze; Levels 4-5, Level 6 and First item to Kassadin; Two+ items back to Ryze. Applied to win[] and phases[].side. Every side matches a caption that was already written.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three errors. (a) Ryze's W and E are swapped everywhere in the content layer: it writes 'Spell Flux (W)' and 'Rune Prison (E)'. Riot has Rune Prison as W (11/10.5/10/9.5/9s, 615 range) and Spell Flux as E (3.5s down to 2.5s, 615 range). (b) The full layer calls Rune Prison a 'point-blank root' in breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d and report[5].t — it is a 615-range targeted cast, not point-blank. (c) The conditional that decides the entire lane was missing: Riot's Rune Prison text is 'traps a target in a cage of runes, damaging them and slowing their movement. If the target has Flux on it, they are instead rooted.' No Flux means no root — just a slow, and Riftwalk leaves through a slow. The pages instead told you to 'sidestep his Flux/Rune Prison root projectiles with the blink', which cannot be done: Rune Prison is a targeted cast.
audit.why: Riot's own W and E descriptions and ranges settle the letters and the range. The Flux condition is stated verbatim in the W tooltip and is the only reason Kassadin has a mid-game window at all.
audit.corrected: Letters corrected to Spell Flux (E) and Rune Prison (W) in early, mid, spikes[0], spikes[1], whys[1], whys[2], whys[4], wants.foe[0] and wants.you[1]. 'Point-blank' replaced with 615 range. The Flux condition is now the headline sequencing rule on both layers: keep Spell Flux off you and Rune Prison only slows, so the blink still works.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2].d offered a 'fifteen-second invitation' after Ryze spends Rune Prison.
audit.why: Rune Prison is 11s at rank 1 falling to 9s. Fifteen seconds does not exist, and the gap is the entire green light for a Riftwalk commit.
audit.corrected: Stated as eleven seconds in dosFull[2], breakdown.cooldowns, spikes[1], mid and report[9].

audit.why: Null Sphere does not silence — Riot's text is 'dealing damage and interrupting channels'.

edits.before: Ryze owns the opening — his Overload (Q) out-ranges and out-paces your short, mana-hungry Null Sphere, and the moment he tags you with Spell Flux (W) and follows with Rune Prison (E) you eat a root plus a full Overload rotation. You have no Nether Blade mana sustain or Force Pulse yet, so do not trade autos into him: soak Null Sphere's 1.5s shield onto his poke when you must step up, and last-hit defensively. Your one comfort is Void Stone's passive already shaving 15% off everything he throws.
edits.after: Ryze owns the opening — his Overload (Q) out-ranges and out-paces your short, mana-hungry Null Sphere, and the moment he tags you with Spell Flux (E) and follows with Rune Prison (W) you eat a root plus a full Overload rotation. Learn that order: Rune Prison only roots a target already carrying Flux, and otherwise just slows. You have no Nether Blade mana or Force Pulse yet, so do not trade autos — soak Null Sphere's shield on his poke and last-hit defensively. Void Stone shaves 15% off everything he throws.

edits.before: This is where the lane flips your way. Nether Blade refunds five-fold mana off champion hits so you stop running dry to his Q-spam, a maxed Null Sphere shield blanks more Overload, and at 6 Riftwalk finally answers him — blink sideways the instant his Flux/Rune Prison lock is incoming and the root whiffs, leaving him on cooldown for a free trade. Bait the root, then Q-blink in: Ryze has no dash and a pre-Seraph's Ryze cannot kill a Kassadin who shrugs off 15% of his damage.
edits.after: This is where the lane flips your way. Nether Blade refunds five-fold mana off champion hits so you stop running dry to his Q-spam, a maxed Null Sphere shield blanks more Overload, and at 6 Riftwalk finally answers him. The sequencing that matters: keep Spell Flux (E) off you and Rune Prison (W) downgrades from a root to a slow, and Riftwalk leaves through a slow. If Flux does land, blink before the W follows — 11s at rank 1 means one whiffed root buys the whole trade. Ryze has no dash to answer you.

edits.before: Be honest with yourself here — Ryze is the rare AP that out-scales even you. Once he stacks Archangel's into Seraph's, his rune-reset Overload chains hit harder and more often than your blink burst can answer in a straight duel, and his Rune Prison still catches you the moment Riftwalk is on cooldown. Void Stone's reduction helps but does not save a 1v1. Use your superior mobility to flank and delete the carries he's protecting and to split, not to fight Ryze head-on — let your team absorb the raid-boss.
edits.after: Be honest with yourself here — Ryze is the rare AP that out-scales even you. Once he stacks Archangel's into Seraph's, his rune-reset Overload chains hit harder and more often than your blink burst can answer in a straight duel, and a Flux-primed Rune Prison still catches you between blinks. Void Stone's reduction helps but does not save a 1v1. Use your superior mobility to flank and delete the carries he's protecting and to split, not to fight Ryze head-on — let your team absorb the raid-boss.

notes: The W/E swap on Ryze is the calibration-grade error in this file: the content layer wrote 'Spell Flux (W)' and 'Rune Prison (E)' consistently, which is backwards, and it also told the reader to sidestep Rune Prison — a targeted cast that cannot be dodged. The real counterplay, Rune Prison rooting only through Flux, was nowhere on the page. Standing kit-flag misfire again: kassadin.json marks Null Sphere as a channel, and _missing-interactions.json produces 'Ryze can cancel your Null Sphere (Q) with Rune Prison (W)' from it. Riot's description says Null Sphere interrupts channels rather than being one, so I did not write that row. Note the same wrong row also exists for the mid-lane copy (kassadin_mid vs ryze) if anyone works that file.
